questions.prompt: A VLA succeeds on 'put the cup on the plate' in 19 of 20 trials in a scene with exactly one cup and one plate. What can you conclude about instruction understanding?
options: That it understands all object-placement instructions, since 95% success covers the task family.
Little: the scene may determine the task without the instruction; a counterfactual instruction test is needed.
That language is irrelevant to the policy, because it succeeded without any extra language data.
That it generalises to new objects and new scenes, because success was this high.
questions.explanation: Success does not show the instruction was used.

questions.prompt: Actions in [-1,1] are quantised into 128 bins. What is the worst-case reconstruction error? (4 decimals)
Bin index of a=0.6 with range [-1,1] and 16 bins (integer, bins numbered from 0)?
A 7-token action is decoded at 28 tokens per second, one action per call. What is the control rate in Hz?
Wilson 95% interval for 8 successes in 10 trials: what is the LOWER bound? (2 decimals)
Which is the best way to attribute a performance drop to 'new objects'?
options: Compare training-scene success with success reported by a different lab on its own held-out scenes.
Compare two policies trained on different data, one on seen objects and one on new objects.
Compare seen and held-out objects in the same scenes with the same instruction template and equal trials.
Use many more trials only on held-out objects, and keep the seen-object trial count small.
questions.explanation: Controls must change one axis at a time.

questions.prompt: Design an experiment to test whether a VLA follows the language instruction rather than the scene layout. Specify the manipulation, metric and what outcome rejects 'it follows the instruction'.
rubric: Holds the scene fixed and varies only the instruction (and the reverse control).
Metric such as action difference or target-object success, with repeated trials.
States in advance a result (e.g. same action for conflicting instructions) that rejects the claim.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.
